title: History Lec 3
summary: Post-Mauryan period: Pushyamitra Shunga (capital Vidisha) killed Brihadratha and founded the Shunga dynasty; Kalidasa's 'Malavikagnimitram' is about his son Agnimitra; Vasudeva killed the last Shunga, Devabhuti, and founded the Kanva dynasty.
Kharavela belonged to the Chedi dynasty (Odisha); the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves are in Odisha, while the Udayagiri caves of Vidisha (M.P.) are different.

Satavahanas: founder Simuka, greatest ruler Gautamiputra Satakarni (mother Gautami Balashri, Nasik Prashasti), capital Pratishthana, port Ghantasala, first land grants, lead and potin coins, metronymic names; called 'Andhra-bhrityas' in the Puranas.
Art schools: Amaravati - white limestone/marble, Mathura - red sandstone (indigenous), Gandhara/Indo-Greek - grey schist; early aniconic depiction of the Buddha (empty throne, Bodhi tree, wheel).

Indo-Greeks: Menander (capital Sakala/Sialkot, Milindapanho - Nagasena), first gold coins; Heliodorus, envoy of Antialcidas, erected the Garuda pillar at Besnagar. Order of arrival: Indo-Greeks, Shakas, Parthians, Kushans.

Shakas: according to the Junagadh inscription, Rudradaman repaired the Sudarshana lake (built by Pushyagupta in Chandragupta Maurya's reign); Kshatrapa system = military governorship; Vikram Samvat 57 BC, Shaka Samvat AD 78.

Kushans: Great Yuezhi, title 'Devaputra', capitals Purushapura and Mathura, Kujula and Vima Kadphises, Kanishka a patron of Buddhism (fourth ruler as per the Rabatak inscription); Gondophernes in the Takht-i-Bahi (Gandhara) inscription.

Sangam: Tamil language, three Sangams (first and third at Madurai, second at Kapatapuram), patrons Pandyas; Tolkappiyam the oldest; Ettuthokai (8) and Pattupattu (10); Akam = love, Puram = war; Silappadikaram (Ilango Adigal) and Manimekalai (Sittalai Sattanar).
Three Tamil kingdoms: Chera (Vanji, bow and arrow, Muziris), Pandya (Madurai, fish, Korkai), Chola (Uraiyur/Puhar, tiger); the Rashtrakutas (Dantidurga, Manyakheta) were not a Tamil kingdom.

Tripartite Struggle (8th-9th century): Palas (east), Pratiharas (west), Rashtrakutas (south) - for Kannauj; Harshavardhana (606-647, Pushyabhuti) wrote Ratnavali, Priyadarshika and Nagananda; Banabhatta wrote Harshacharita and Kadambari; Pulakeshin II defeated Harsha on the Narmada.
Universities: Nalanda - Kumaragupta I (destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji), Vikramashila - Dharmapala, Odantapuri - Gopala (founder of the Pala dynasty); Gurjara-Pratiharas: Mihira Bhoja the greatest.

Chola administration was decentralised: Ur (common villagers) and Sabha (Brahmins), election system known from the Uttaramerur inscription; grants: Shalabhoga, Devadana, Brahmadeya, Pallichchandam; taxes: Vetti (forced labour), Kadamai; Vijayalaya built the Nishumbhasudini temple; Rajendra I conquered Srivijaya (Shailendras).

Travellers: Fa-Hien (Chandragupta II), Hiuen Tsang (Harsha; Si-Yu-Ki), Ibn Battuta (Morocco; Tughlaq), Paes and Barbosa (Portugal; Krishnadeva Raya), Megasthenes (Chandragupta); Kalhana - Rajatarangini; Periplus 1st century AD.

Temple styles: Nagara (north; shikhara-amalaka-kalasha, jagati), Dravida (Pallavas; vimana, gopuram, gajaprishtha), Vesara (Chalukyas), Kalinga (rekha/pidha/khakhara deul, jagamohana); Sandhara = inner circumambulatory path, Nirandhara = outer.

Pallavas: founder Simhavishnu, capital Kanchi; Mahendra style, Mamalla style (Pancha Rathas), Rajasimha style (Shore Temple, Kailasanatha); Chola temples: Brihadeeswara - Rajaraja I, Gangaikonda Cholapuram - Rajendra I, Airavatesvara - Rajaraja II.

Caves: Ajanta - 30 (Buddhist), Ellora - 34 (all three religions, Kailasa temple in Cave 16, Krishna I), Elephanta - Trimurti, Undavalli - reclining Vishnu, Bhimbetka (M.P.); literature: Natyashastra - Bharata Muni, Ashtadhyayi - Panini, Gita Govinda - Jayadeva; instruments: Ghana, Sushira, Tata, Avanaddha.

mcqs.q: After the decline of the Mauryan Empire, the commander Pushyamitra killed the last Mauryan ruler and founded which dynasty?
mcqs.e: Pushyamitra Shunga killed the last Mauryan ruler Brihadratha and founded the Shunga dynasty.

mcqs.q: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
mcqs.e: Brihadratha was killed by his commander Pushyamitra Shunga.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Pushyamitra Shunga's son?
mcqs.e: Kalidasa wrote the play 'Malavikagnimitram' with Agnimitra as its hero.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Malavikagnimitram'?
mcqs.e: It is a romantic play whose hero is the Shunga ruler Agnimitra.

mcqs.q: Who was the last ruler of the Shunga dynasty?
mcqs.e: Devabhuti was killed by his minister Vasudeva.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Kanva dynasty by killing Devabhuti, the last Shunga ruler?
mcqs.e: Vasudeva was the founder of the Kanva dynasty.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled Magadha after the Shungas?
mcqs.e: The Kanvas followed the Shungas, and the Satavahanas came to power after the Kanvas.

mcqs.q: Who were the Kushans?
mcqs.e: The Kushans were a branch of the 'Great Yuezhi' tribe.

mcqs.q: Which city was the capital of Pushyamitra Shunga?
mcqs.e: Pushyamitra was a follower of Brahmanism and made Vidisha an important seat of power.

mcqs.q: Patanjali, the author of the Mahabhashya, was a contemporary of whom?
mcqs.e: Patanjali wrote the Mahabhashya during the Shunga period.

mcqs.q: King Kharavela belonged to which dynasty?
mcqs.e: Kharavela ruled Kalinga (Odisha); the Hathigumpha inscription is associated with him.

mcqs.q: In which state are the Udayagiri-Khandagiri caves (associated with Kharavela) located?
mcqs.e: The Udayagiri caves near Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh are different (Gupta period).

mcqs.q: Which dynasty first started the practice of granting land to Brahmins?
mcqs.e: The Satavahanas granted land to Brahmins and Buddhist monks and patronised Brahmanism.

mcqs.q: Who was the founder of the Satavahana dynasty?
mcqs.e: Simuka established Satavahana power by overthrowing the last Kanva ruler.

mcqs.q: Who is considered the greatest ruler of the Satavahana dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Nasik Prashasti, issued by his mother Gautami Balashri, records his achievements.

mcqs.q: By what name are the Satavahanas referred to in the Puranas?
mcqs.e: The Puranas mention the Satavahanas as 'Andhra-bhrityas'.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Satavahanas?
mcqs.e: Pratishthana is modern Paithan in Maharashtra.

mcqs.q: What does the use of the mother's name in the names of Satavahana kings indicate?
mcqs.e: Examples include Gautamiputra and Vashishthiputra.

mcqs.q: What was the name of Gautamiputra Satakarni's mother?
mcqs.e: She recorded his achievements in the Nasik inscription.

mcqs.q: Which ancient port of Andhra Pradesh was famous during the Satavahana period?
mcqs.e: Ghantasala was a port under Satavahana control.

mcqs.q: What was an 'Ahara' or 'Rashtra' in the Satavahana period?
mcqs.e: Ahara/Rashtra denoted a district in Satavahana administration.

mcqs.q: The Satavahanas issued coins mainly of which metals?
mcqs.e: Coins of lead and potin (an alloy of copper, tin and lead) are their hallmark.

mcqs.q: Which Satavahana ruler was defeated by the Shaka ruler Rudradaman I?
mcqs.e: Rudradaman was a Shaka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler.

mcqs.q: The Amaravati Stupa was mainly built under which dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Ikshvakus later carried the work forward.

mcqs.q: Which stone was mainly used in the Amaravati school of art?
mcqs.e: White limestone is characteristic of the Amaravati school.

mcqs.q: Which stone was mainly used in the Mathura school of art?
mcqs.e: The Mathura school was wholly indigenous and flourished under the Kushans.

mcqs.q: Which stone was mainly used in the Indo-Greek (Gandhara) school of art?
mcqs.e: It is also called Graeco-Buddhist or Hellenistic art.

mcqs.q: How was the Buddha depicted in 'aniconic' representation?
o: Through symbols like an empty throne, Bodhi tree and wheel
mcqs.e: Aniconic means non-human (symbolic) representation.

mcqs.q: The Ikshvakus ruled the Krishna-Godavari delta of the eastern Deccan after the decline of which dynasty?
mcqs.e: Nagarjunakonda is associated with the Ikshvakus.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Kadamba dynasty (Banavasi)?
mcqs.e: Mayurasharman founded the kingdom after avenging an insult by the Pallavas; the capital was Banavasi.

mcqs.q: Pulakeshin II defeated which famous North Indian ruler on the banks of the Narmada?
mcqs.e: After this victory Pulakeshin took the title 'Dakshinapatheshvara'.

mcqs.q: Who was ruling Magadha when Alexander invaded India (326 BC)?
mcqs.e: Alexander never reached Magadha; he fought Porus.

mcqs.q: Which Indian king did Alexander defeat and then return his kingdom to him?
mcqs.e: Porus was defeated in the Battle of the Hydaspes (Jhelum).

mcqs.q: Which general of Alexander founded the Seleucid dynasty?
mcqs.e: Seleucus later fought Chandragupta Maurya.

mcqs.q: Who was the most famous Indo-Greek ruler of ancient India?
mcqs.e: Pushyamitra Shunga and Rudradaman were not Indo-Greeks.

mcqs.q: In 'Milindapanho', whom did Milinda (Menander) put his questions to?
mcqs.e: Milindapanho means 'The Questions of Milinda'.

mcqs.q: Where was Menander's capital?
mcqs.e: Sakala is modern Sialkot.

mcqs.q: Which rulers were the first to issue gold coins in India?
mcqs.e: The Indo-Greeks also issued coins bearing portraits of kings.

mcqs.q: Who erected the Garuda pillar (Garudadhvaja) at Besnagar (Vidisha)?
mcqs.e: Heliodorus was the envoy of the Indo-Greek king Antialcidas and a devotee of Vasudeva (Krishna).

mcqs.q: Heliodorus was the envoy of which Indo-Greek ruler?
mcqs.e: He adopted the Bhagavata faith and became a devotee of Vasudeva.

mcqs.q: What is the correct order in which groups from Central Asia came to India?
mcqs.e: All of them were later assimilated into Indian society.

mcqs.q: What was the effect of foreign rulers from Central Asia (Shakas, Kushans, etc.) on Indian society?
o: They were assimilated into Indian society
mcqs.e: They adopted Hinduism or Buddhism.

mcqs.q: Which Shaka ruler repaired the Sudarshana lake without imposing any tax?
mcqs.e: This is known from the Junagadh (Girnar) rock inscription in Gujarat.

mcqs.q: Who built the Sudarshana lake?
mcqs.e: It was later repaired under Ashoka, Rudradaman and Skandagupta.

mcqs.q: The Takht-i-Bahi inscription is related to which region?
mcqs.e: It is in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (Pakistan) and is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

mcqs.q: Which Parthian ruler is mentioned in the Takht-i-Bahi inscription?
mcqs.e: Gondophernes was a Parthian (Indo-Parthian) ruler.

mcqs.q: Which rulers adopted the title 'Devaputra'?
mcqs.e: The title signified a claim to divine origin.

mcqs.q: By what other name are the Kushans known?
mcqs.e: They were the last of the major Central Asian groups to come to India.

mcqs.q: What was the first capital of the Kushans?
mcqs.e: Mathura later became their second capital.

mcqs.q: Who was the first ruler of the Kushan dynasty?
mcqs.e: He was succeeded by Vima Takto and then Vima Kadphises.

mcqs.q: What does the Rabatak inscription (Afghanistan) reveal about Kanishka?
o: He was the fourth Kushan ruler
mcqs.e: It lists Kujula Kadphises, Vima Takto and Vima Kadphises as Kanishka's predecessors.

mcqs.q: Kanishka was a patron of which religion?
mcqs.e: The Fourth Buddhist Council (Kashmir) was held under his patronage.

mcqs.q: When did the Vikram Samvat begin?
mcqs.e: Traditionally linked to King Vikramaditya of Ujjain defeating the Shakas.

mcqs.q: When did the Shaka Samvat begin?
mcqs.e: It is linked to Kanishka's accession and is the basis of India's national calendar.

mcqs.q: Why was the Shaka era not called the 'Kushan era'?
o: The Shakas were the first kings
All foreigners from Central Asia were called 'Shakas'
mcqs.e: The Shaka era began in AD 78.

mcqs.q: What was the 'Kshatrapa system' of the Shaka satraps?
o: Military governorship - the military chief ruled the province
mcqs.e: Provinces were governed by military governors (Kshatrapas and Mahakshatrapas).

mcqs.q: Uttarapatha was a trade route connecting which regions?
o: The north-west with northern India and onward to the south
mcqs.e: Uttarapatha linked the north-west with northern and southern India.

mcqs.q: Sangam literature was mainly written in which language?
mcqs.e: The Sangam age is placed roughly between the 3rd century BC and the 3rd century AD.

mcqs.q: What does 'Sangam' mean?
o: An academy/assembly of Tamil poets and scholars
mcqs.e: Three Sangams are traditionally recognised.

mcqs.q: How many Sangams are traditionally believed to have been held?
mcqs.e: The first and third were held at Madurai and the second at Kapatapuram.

mcqs.q: Where was the second Sangam held?
mcqs.e: Tolkappiyam is believed to have been composed during this Sangam.

mcqs.q: Who patronised all three Sangams?
mcqs.e: The Pandya capital was Madurai.

mcqs.q: Which is considered the oldest Tamil text?
mcqs.e: It is a work on Tamil grammar attributed to Tolkappiyar.

mcqs.q: Which culture prevailed in South India around 1000 BC?
mcqs.e: Large stones were placed around burial sites.

mcqs.q: By what name were the Chera rulers of Kerala referred to in Ashoka's inscriptions?
mcqs.e: The Chera emblem was the bow and arrow.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was NOT a Tamil kingdom?
mcqs.e: The Rashtrakutas belonged to the Karnataka/Maharashtra region.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Chera kingdom?
mcqs.e: Vanji is often identified with Karur.

mcqs.q: What was the royal emblem of the Cheras?
mcqs.e: The Pandya emblem was the fish.

mcqs.q: What was the royal emblem of the Pandyas?
mcqs.e: The Pandya capital was Madurai.

mcqs.q: What was the royal emblem of the Cholas?
mcqs.e: The early capital of the Sangam-age Cholas was Uraiyur.

mcqs.q: By what other name is the Chola port of 'Puhar' known?
mcqs.e: Puhar was situated at the mouth of the Kaveri.

mcqs.q: Which was the chief port of the Pandyas?
mcqs.e: Korkai was famous for pearls.

mcqs.q: Which was the chief port of the Cheras?
mcqs.e: Muziris was a centre of Roman trade; Tondi was another Chera port.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Rashtrakuta dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Rashtrakuta capital was Manyakheta (Malkhed).

mcqs.q: Where was the capital of the Rashtrakutas?
mcqs.e: The Rashtrakutas built the Kailasa temple at Ellora.

mcqs.q: By what name are the eight anthologies of ancient Tamil literature known?
mcqs.e: Ettu = eight, thokai = anthology.

mcqs.q: What is Pattupattu?
mcqs.e: Ettuthokai and Pattupattu are the main anthologies of Sangam literature.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Silappadikaram'?
mcqs.e: It is one of the Five Great Epics of Tamil literature.

mcqs.q: The story of 'Silappadikaram' is based on which characters?
mcqs.e: Kovalan fell for the dancer Madhavi; Kannagi is worshipped as a goddess of chastity.

mcqs.q: Why was Kovalan sentenced to death?
o: On a false charge of stealing the queen's anklet
mcqs.e: He was wrongly suspected while selling Kannagi's anklet; Kannagi's curse destroyed Madurai.

mcqs.q: What was the name of the daughter of Kovalan and Madhavi?
mcqs.e: The epic Manimekalai is based on her.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the epic 'Manimekalai'?
mcqs.e: It is also counted among the Five Great Epics of Tamil.

mcqs.q: In Sangam literature, the theme 'Akam' relates to what?
mcqs.e: 'Puram' relates to heroism and war.

mcqs.q: In Sangam literature, the theme 'Puram' relates to what?
o: War, valour and praise of kings
mcqs.e: Akam deals with the inner (love) life; Puram with the outer (public) life.

mcqs.q: What is the main theme of Purananuru and Patirruppattu?
mcqs.e: These are Puram-based works of the Ettuthokai.

mcqs.q: In Sangam literature, what were ordinary ploughmen called?
mcqs.e: Large landowners were called Vellalar.

mcqs.q: In Sangam literature, what were large landowners called?
mcqs.e: The term Adimai was used for slaves/landless labourers.

mcqs.q: Adichanallur in Tamil Nadu is famous for remains of which period?
mcqs.e: The site helps in understanding early Tamil (Sangam) culture.

mcqs.q: The 'Tripartite Struggle' of the 8th-9th centuries was fought among which powers?
mcqs.e: It was fought for control of Kannauj, with no decisive winner.

mcqs.q: The Tripartite Struggle was fought for control of which city?
mcqs.e: Kannauj was a symbol of imperial prestige in North India.

mcqs.q: Which was the eastern power in the Tripartite Struggle?
mcqs.e: The Pratiharas were in the west and the Rashtrakutas in the south.

mcqs.q: Kannauj became famous as the capital of which ruler?
mcqs.e: Harsha is counted among the greatest rulers of North India.

mcqs.q: What was the reign period of Harshavardhana?
mcqs.e: Harsha belonged to the Pushyabhuti (Vardhana) dynasty.

mcqs.q: Harshavardhana belonged to which dynasty?
mcqs.e: His capital was later shifted from Thanesar to Kannauj.

mcqs.q: Which three plays were written by Harshavardhana?
mcqs.e: Harsha was himself a poet and dramatist.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Harshacharita', the biography of Harshavardhana?
mcqs.e: Banabhatta was Harsha's court poet and also wrote 'Kadambari'.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Kadambari'?
mcqs.e: Banabhatta was the court poet of Harshavardhana.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the greatest ruler of the Gurjara-Pratihara dynasty?
mcqs.e: Nagabhata I was the early powerful ruler of this dynasty.

mcqs.q: Gopala was the founder of which dynasty?
mcqs.e: According to tradition, he built the Odantapuri university.

mcqs.q: According to tradition, who built the Odantapuri university?
mcqs.e: It was located in Bihar.

mcqs.q: Which city was the capital of the Gurjara-Pratihara ruler Vatsaraja?
mcqs.e: The early Pratiharas ruled from Avanti (Ujjain); Nagabhata II later shifted to Kannauj.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Vikramashila university near Bhagalpur (Bihar)?
mcqs.e: Dharmapala was a ruler of the Pala dynasty.

mcqs.q: Who founded Nalanda University?
mcqs.e: It was destroyed by Bakhtiyar Khalji.

mcqs.q: Who destroyed Nalanda University?
mcqs.e: The event is dated to around AD 1193.

mcqs.q: In Pallava administration, what was the smallest self-governing unit at the village level?
mcqs.e: Hierarchy: Ur (village) - Nadu (taluk) - Kottam/Vishaya - Mandalam.

mcqs.q: In South Indian administrative units, what level was a 'Nadu'?
mcqs.e: Above the Nadu were the Kottam (Vishaya) and then the Mandalam.

mcqs.q: Who administered a Vishaya (Kottam)?
mcqs.e: The Mandalam was the highest unit.

mcqs.q: In South Indian village committees, what was the function of the 'Eri Variyam'?
mcqs.e: The committee for justice was called the 'Nyaya (Dharma) Variyam'.

mcqs.q: Rajendra Chola I is famous for which expedition?
o: Naval expedition against the Srivijaya empire
mcqs.e: Srivijaya, in the Indonesia-Malaya region, was ruled by the Shailendra dynasty.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty ruled the Srivijaya empire?
mcqs.e: It was located in present-day Indonesia.

mcqs.q: Rajendra Chola I was a contemporary of which ruler of Ghazni?
mcqs.e: Rajendra I ruled from AD 1014 to 1044.

mcqs.q: Who was the father of Rajendra Chola I?
mcqs.e: Rajaraja I ruled from AD 985 to 1014.

mcqs.q: What kind of administration did the Cholas have?
mcqs.e: Villages had assemblies such as the Ur and the Sabha.

mcqs.q: What was the difference between the 'Ur' and the 'Sabha' in a Chola village?
o: Ur was of Brahmins and Sabha of common people
Ur was an assembly of common villagers and Sabha of learned Brahmins
mcqs.e: Details of elections and functioning come from the Uttaramerur inscription.

mcqs.q: Which inscription provides information about the Chola electoral system?
mcqs.e: It is in Tamil Nadu; members were chosen by lot (kudavolai system).

mcqs.q: In the Chola period, what was a land grant made to schools called?
mcqs.e: Shalabhoga was land granted for the maintenance of schools.

mcqs.q: In the Chola period, what was a land grant made to temples called?
mcqs.e: Devadana was land granted to temples.

mcqs.q: In the Chola period, what was a land grant made to Brahmins called?
mcqs.e: Brahmadeya villages were granted to Brahmins.

mcqs.q: In the Chola period, what was a land grant made to Jain institutions called?
mcqs.e: Remember: Shalabhoga - schools, Devadana - temples, Brahmadeya - Brahmins, Pallichchandam - Jains.

mcqs.q: In what form was the Chola-period levy 'Vetti' collected?
mcqs.e: Vetti was taken in the form of forced labour.

mcqs.q: What was 'Kadamai' in the Chola period?
mcqs.e: Kadamai was related to land revenue.

mcqs.q: Who is regarded as the most celebrated ruler of the early (Sangam-age) Cholas?
mcqs.e: Karikala is known for the Battle of Venni and building embankments on the Kaveri.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Imperial Chola dynasty?
mcqs.e: Vijayalaya revived Chola power in the 9th century.

mcqs.q: Vijayalaya Chola captured the Kaveri delta by defeating whom?
mcqs.e: The Muttaraiyars were feudatories of the Pallavas.

mcqs.q: Vijayalaya Chola built a temple for which goddess?
mcqs.e: The temple was built at Thanjavur.

mcqs.q: Which of the following was a title of Rajaraja I?
mcqs.e: He built the Brihadeeswara (Rajarajeshwaram) temple at Thanjavur.

mcqs.q: What was the reign period of Rajendra Chola I?
mcqs.e: He was preceded by Rajaraja I (AD 985-1014).

mcqs.q: Which Rashtrakuta ruler defeated the Chola ruler Parantaka I?
mcqs.e: Krishna III won the Battle of Takkolam and built the Krishneshvara temple at Rameswaram.

mcqs.q: In which century was 'The Periplus of the Erythraean Sea' written?
mcqs.e: Its author is unknown, probably a Greek sailor from Egypt.

mcqs.q: Which Chinese traveller visited the court of Harshavardhana?
mcqs.e: Hiuen Tsang is also spelt Xuanzang.

mcqs.q: During whose reign did Fa-Hien visit India?
mcqs.e: Fa-Hien was the first well-known Chinese pilgrim to visit during the Gupta period.

mcqs.q: What is the name of Hiuen Tsang's book?
mcqs.e: It is also known as 'Great Tang Records on the Western Regions'.

mcqs.q: Who defeated Pulakeshin II?
mcqs.e: Narasimhavarman took the title 'Vatapikonda'.

mcqs.q: Which Pallava ruler was defeated by Pulakeshin II?
mcqs.e: His son Narasimhavarman I avenged the defeat.

mcqs.q: Which title did Narasimhavarman I adopt after defeating Pulakeshin II?
mcqs.e: Vatapi was the capital of the Chalukyas.

mcqs.q: Which title did Pulakeshin II adopt after defeating Harshavardhana?
mcqs.e: The title means 'Lord of the South (Dakshinapatha)'.

mcqs.q: During whose reign did Hiuen Tsang visit Kashmir?
mcqs.e: Durlabhavardhana was the founder of the Karkota dynasty of Kashmir.

mcqs.q: Durlabhavardhana belonged to which dynasty?
mcqs.e: The Karkota dynasty ruled Kashmir.

mcqs.q: Where was the capital of the Maitraka dynasty?
mcqs.e: Hiuen Tsang mentions the Maitraka ruler Shiladitya.

mcqs.q: Harshavardhana's daughter was married to which Maitraka ruler?
mcqs.e: The Maitrakas ruled the Gujarat-Saurashtra region.

mcqs.q: The Ajanta caves are described in the account of which traveller?
mcqs.e: Hiuen Tsang described the Buddhist monastery at Ajanta.

mcqs.q: Ibn Battuta came from which country and visited India during which Sultan's reign?
mcqs.e: His travelogue is called the 'Rihla'.

mcqs.q: Megasthenes came to the court of which ruler?
mcqs.e: He was the ambassador of Seleucus Nicator.

mcqs.q: Domingo Paes and Duarte Barbosa came from which country and visited during whose reign?
mcqs.e: They left accounts of the Vijayanagara Empire.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Rajatarangini'?
mcqs.e: It is a history of the kings of Kashmir.

mcqs.q: Which temple architecture style is mainly found in North India?
mcqs.e: The Nagara style developed from the Gupta period.

mcqs.q: Who developed the Dravida temple style?
mcqs.e: The temples of Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram are examples of Pallava art.

mcqs.q: The Vesara style is a blend of which two styles, and who developed it?
mcqs.e: Aihole, Badami and Pattadakal are its examples.

mcqs.q: The temples of Pattadakal, Aihole and Badami belong to which style?
mcqs.e: They are located in Karnataka.

mcqs.q: Who composed the Aihole inscription (prashasti)?
mcqs.e: Ravikirti was the court poet of Pulakeshin II.

mcqs.q: Which of the following temples is an example of the Dravida style?
mcqs.e: Konark and Lingaraja are Kalinga style; Kandariya Mahadeva is Nagara style.

mcqs.q: What is the innermost chamber housing the main deity in a Hindu temple called?
mcqs.e: It is also called the sanctum sanctorum.

mcqs.q: In the Nagara style, what is the tower-like structure above the garbhagriha called?
mcqs.e: Above the shikhara come the amalaka, kalasha and flag, in that order.

mcqs.q: What is the amla-shaped (gooseberry-shaped) stone disc at the top of a Nagara shikhara called?
mcqs.e: The kalasha sits above the amalaka, with a flag above it.

mcqs.q: What is the raised platform on which a temple stands called?
mcqs.e: Nagara temples are usually built on a raised platform.

mcqs.q: In the Dravida style, what is the stepped pyramidal tower above the garbhagriha called?
mcqs.e: In Dravida temples the tower over the sanctum is the vimana.

mcqs.q: What is the tall gateway at the entrance of Dravida temples called?
mcqs.e: Gopurams are found in South Indian temples, not in North India.

mcqs.q: In Kalinga architecture, what is the assembly hall (mandapa) of the temple called?
mcqs.e: The Kalinga style is the temple style of Odisha.

mcqs.q: In the Kalinga style, what is the tall curvilinear tower called?
mcqs.e: The pyramidal-roofed hall is called the pidha deul.

mcqs.q: In the Kalinga style, what is the pyramidal-roofed hall called?
mcqs.e: A structure with a rectangular base and wagon-vaulted roof is called a khakhara deul.

mcqs.q: In the Kalinga style, what is the structure with a rectangular base and wagon-vaulted roof called?
mcqs.e: Keyword for khakhara deul: wagon-shaped roof.

mcqs.q: In Dravida temple architecture, what is the plan shaped like an elephant's back called?
mcqs.e: Gajaprishtha means 'back of an elephant'.

mcqs.q: In which architectural style is the Sun Temple of Konark built?
mcqs.e: The temple is designed as a chariot drawn by seven horses.

mcqs.q: How many wheels does the chariot of the Konark Sun Temple have?
mcqs.e: The 24 wheels are often linked to the hours of the day and the 7 horses to the days of the week.

mcqs.q: Where is the Kandariya Mahadeva Temple located?
mcqs.e: It is a Nagara-style temple built by the Chandelas.

mcqs.q: Where is the Lingaraja Temple located?
mcqs.e: It is a Kalinga-style temple.

mcqs.q: The Pallava-era Pancha Rathas of Mahabalipuram are carved out of which stone?
mcqs.e: They are monolithic rock-cut temples.

mcqs.q: Who founded the Pallava dynasty (as a major power)?
mcqs.e: The capital was Kanchipuram.

mcqs.q: What was the capital of the Pallavas?
mcqs.e: Kanchi has been a centre of learning since ancient times.

mcqs.q: The Mahendra style is named after which Pallava ruler?
mcqs.e: Early rock-cut cave temples were built in this style.

mcqs.q: The Pancha Rathas of Mahabalipuram were built during the reign of which Pallava ruler?
mcqs.e: The Pancha Rathas and the 'Arjuna's Penance' relief belong to the Mamalla style.

mcqs.q: By what other name is Narasimhavarman I known?
mcqs.e: Hence Mahabalipuram is also called 'Mamallapuram'.

mcqs.q: Who built the Shore Temple at Mahabalipuram?
mcqs.e: Rajasimha also built the Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram.

mcqs.q: The Kailasanatha temple at Kanchipuram is built of which stone?
mcqs.e: It is an example of the Rajasimha style.

mcqs.q: Who built the Brihadeeswara Temple at Thanjavur?
mcqs.e: It is also called the Rajarajeshwaram temple.

mcqs.q: Who built the Brihadeeswara Temple at Gangaikonda Cholapuram?
mcqs.e: Rajendra Chola is sometimes called the 'Napoleon of South India'.

mcqs.q: Who built the Airavatesvara Temple?
mcqs.e: All three Chola temples are UNESCO sites as the 'Great Living Chola Temples'.

mcqs.q: Which temples are included in the 'Great Living Chola Temples'?
mcqs.e: All are outstanding examples of Chola architecture.

mcqs.q: Which dynasty built the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh?
mcqs.e: This Gupta-period temple is in Uttar Pradesh.

mcqs.q: A temple with a circumambulatory path inside, around the garbhagriha, is called what?
mcqs.e: If the path is outside the garbhagriha, it is called Nirandhara.

mcqs.q: A temple with a circumambulatory path outside the garbhagriha is called what?
mcqs.e: Remember: inside - Sandhara, outside - Nirandhara.

mcqs.q: In which state are the Kanheri, Karla and Bhaja caves located?
mcqs.e: These caves were excavated for Buddhist monks.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between Chaitya and Vihara caves?
o: Chaitya is a residence and Vihara a place of worship
Chaitya is a place of worship and Vihara a residence
mcqs.e: Vihara caves served as monasteries for monks.

mcqs.q: In which state are the Bhimbetka rock shelters (prehistoric cave paintings) located?
mcqs.e: They are near Bhopal.

mcqs.q: How many caves are there in total at Ajanta (including the unfinished one)?
mcqs.e: Remember: 29 + 1 unfinished = 30.

mcqs.q: How many caves are there in total at Ellora?
mcqs.e: The Ellora caves belong to Hinduism, Buddhism and Jainism.

mcqs.q: The construction of the Ellora caves is mainly credited to whom?
mcqs.e: Ajanta is mainly credited to the Satavahanas and Vakatakas.

mcqs.q: The Ajanta caves are associated with which religion?
mcqs.e: The famous 'Flying Apsara' painting is at Ajanta.

mcqs.q: The 'Flying Apsara' painting is a masterpiece of which cave group?
mcqs.e: Ajanta is famous for its murals.

mcqs.q: In which cave is the Kailasa temple of Ellora, and who built it?
mcqs.e: It is a monolithic temple carved top-down out of a single rock.

mcqs.q: In which caves is the famous Trimurti sculpture found?
mcqs.e: Elephanta is on an island near Mumbai and is dedicated to Shiva.

mcqs.q: Where are the Undavalli caves, known for the reclining Vishnu on Sheshanaga, located?
mcqs.e: The cave is famous for its monolithic reclining Vishnu.

mcqs.q: Which stories are carved on the toranas (gateways) of the Sanchi Stupa?
mcqs.e: Jataka tales are stories of the Buddha's previous births.

mcqs.q: Who built the Sanchi Stupa and who enlarged it?
mcqs.e: Sanchi has four toranas (gateways).

mcqs.q: How many recognised styles (pathas) of Vedic chanting are there in total?
mcqs.e: They are divided into Prakriti pathas and Vikriti pathas.

mcqs.q: Which music style was considered formal and divine in ancient India?
mcqs.e: Gandharva music was regarded as sacred and divine.

mcqs.q: What is called the 'Fifth Veda'?
mcqs.e: It was composed by Bharata Muni.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the Natyashastra?
mcqs.e: It is an ancient treatise on drama and performing arts.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the Ashtadhyayi?
mcqs.e: The Ashtadhyayi is the foundational text of Sanskrit grammar.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Gita Govinda'?
mcqs.e: Jayadeva was the court poet of Lakshmana Sena of the Sena dynasty of Bengal.

mcqs.q: What are solid instruments (like cymbals, ghatam and bells) called?
mcqs.e: Solid instruments made from everyday objects are called Ghana vadya.

mcqs.q: What are wind instruments such as the flute and shehnai called?
mcqs.e: Sushira = played by blowing air.

mcqs.q: What are stringed instruments such as the sitar and veena called?
mcqs.e: Tata = stringed instruments.

mcqs.q: What are percussion instruments with a stretched leather membrane (dholak, tabla) called?
mcqs.e: They are membranophone (percussion) instruments.

mcqs.q: Who wrote the play 'Mudrarakshasa'?
mcqs.e: Though set in the Mauryan period, it was written much later (Gupta age).

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Mrichchhakatikam' (The Little Clay Cart)?
mcqs.e: It is a famous Sanskrit play.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Abhijnanashakuntalam'?
mcqs.e: It is Kalidasa's most famous play.

mcqs.q: Who wrote 'Svapnavasavadattam'?
mcqs.e: Bhasa is one of the earliest known Sanskrit dramatists.
